title: Canary rollout scratchpad - model v2.3.1
content:
Context: quick scratchpad for rolling out model v2.3.1 to hosted-api. This is a personal working doc - rough checklist + guardrails. Primary goals: 1) validate quality/regression on golden prompts and customers, 2) keep latency and error budget within SLO, 3) test fallback behavior and version pinning.

Background:
- v2.3.1: tokenizer fix + attention kernel change + quantization profile B. Baseline: v2.2.8 in production.
- Perf expectations: p95 latency should be <= current + 120ms; token cost ~same or slightly lower.

Quick rollout plan (high-level):
1) Canary 1% (30m warm + 60m observe) -> 5% (1h observe) -> 20% (2h observe) -> 50% (3h observe) -> 100%
2) Stop or rollback if any guardrail trips.

Detailed steps / commands:
- Create canary rollout (console): Redwood Console -> Models -> v2.3.1 -> Start Canary
- CLI: rdm rollout create --model v2.3.1 --strategy canary --steps "1:30m,5:1h,20:2h,50:3h" --metrics error_rate,p95_latency,model_regressions
- Tag rollout with JIRA-8742 / PR #1428 and record in confluence page above.

Metrics to monitor (primary):
- Error rate (5xx / client errors) absolute increase >0.3pp OR relative >50% over baseline -> FAIL
- p95 latency increase >200ms absolute OR >30% relative -> FAIL
- Throughput drop / queueing: consumer backlog > 10% sustained -> investigate
- Quality regressions: evaluation on golden prompt set (10 prompts) -> any regression in correctness/ hallucination score >2 points -> FAIL
- Cost per token deviation >+15% -> flag but allow short investigate window

SLO/guardrail thresholds (quick):
- Error rate delta threshold: +0.3 percentage points
- p95 latency delta: +200ms
- Golden prompt regression threshold: metric drop >2 points

Rollout owner/responsibilities:
- Primary owner: Zoe Ramirez (monitoring + rollback authority)
- Secondary: Alex Garcia (infra, autoscale & kernel tuning)
- Quality lead: Maya Singh (golden prompt checks & evals)
- On-call SRE: Samir Patel (alerts & incident)

Runbook (if alarm fires):
1) Pause rollout (console or CLI).
2) Scale dedicated capacity / increase burst if bottleneck suspected (notify Alex).
3) If quality regressions: revert to v2.2.8 for canary and open hotfix PR.
4) Notify #eng-release, #customer-ops, and attach snapshot of traces + failing prompts.
5) If unknown, rollback to previous stable and schedule canary again after root cause.

Version pinning notes (customers):
- Default behavior: customers on hosted-api receive latest stable by default.
- For customers who pin: store mapping customer_id -> pinned_model_version in config-store. Verify that rollback correctly honors pinned mappings.
- Test: simulate pinned customer in canary traffic slice (add header X-Redwood-Customer:test-pinned) and ensure traffic uses pinned version and is unaffected by canary.

Observability queries (placeholders):
- Error rate: sum(rate(requests{status=~"5.."}[1m])) / sum(rate(requests[1m]))
- p95 latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le))
- Golden prompt eval: run nightly eval job against eval-suite/canary-golden-2026-02

Notes / TODO / follow-ups:
- TODO: add canary traffic tagging to make it easier to slice queries (tag: rollout_id=v2.3.1-canary).
- TODO: coordinate with CS for any impacted customers (esp. enterprise pinned ones).
- Check PR #1428 for any config changes that affect routing.
- Follow-up: run full regression suite after 50% step before final cutover.

Risks: kernel change might expose memory pressure on older GPU drivers - have Samir and infra on standby to revert nodes or change kernel selection policy.

Scratch notes (commands I ran locally):
- local eval: python eval/run.py --model models/v2.3.1 --suite eval/golden --output /tmp/v231-canary.json
- quick sanity curl: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" -H "X-Redwood-Canary:v2.3.1" -d '{"prompt":"Explain recursion"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

End of scratchpad. Will tidy and move key steps to confluence once canary is green.
